reviewer: reviewer 1: Claude, an AI assistant and the author of the system. Not a human reader. Human review was not conducted and is outside the scope of this experiment.

rubric.1: Is every factual claim supported by the cited evidence?
rubric.2: Does every citation actually support the claim it is attached to?
rubric.3: Are the cited line ranges correct?
rubric.4: Are there factual claims without a citation?
rubric.5: (abstentions only) Did it abstain correctly, `missing` naming a real gap?

note: Made before any other reader's labels existed (there are none). null = not applicable. Standard as in M13: a citation that supports nothing of its claim (for example the definition of a function cited for 'is called by') is UNCERTAIN; support through structure (graph) metadata counts as support but is noted.

reasons.2: The claim 'called by Scaffold.__init__' rests on the structure line of E1 (called_by sansio/scaffold.py::Scaffold.__init__, line 96); the cited chunk is the callee's definition and contains no call. Structure data counts as metadata of the cited item (plan section 5), so item 1 is PASS.
E1c (Flask.wsgi_app) shows the call; E1, also cited, is the definition of full_dispatch_request and shows no caller.
E1 (the definition of create_url_adapter) is cited with the callers' chunks for 'is called by'; it shows no call. E1b and E2 show the calls.

reasons.1: '...adds a lambda that invokes s.add_url_rule when the blueprint is registered': the cited code shows self.record(lambda s: ...) but not when the recorded function runs.
The render_template calls are shown, but calling a test blueprint's template 'the admin dashboard UI' is a characterisation the cited code does not support.
reasons.5: Should have abstained: Flask has no built-in admin dashboard; the answer is about a test application (tests/test_apps/blueprintapp). Same failure as in M13.

reasons.1: The claim says database migrations are applied by init_db. The cited text only says init_db clears existing data and creates tables from schema.sql; it never mentions migrations, and dropping data is not applying a migration.
reasons.2: The citation describes init_db correctly but does not support the claim that this is how migrations are applied.
reasons.5: Should have abstained (Flask has no database migrations). New in M14: the M13 baseline abstained on this question.
